title: What Are Directives? 🗺️
description: Learn what directives are, the two main categories, and how they extend HTML.

slides.title: Directives: The Secret Sauce of Angular Templates 🧙
slides.content:
# Beyond Plain HTML

A **directive** is a class that can modify the structure of the DOM or change the appearance/behavior of elements.

While a component is a directive with a template, there are two other kinds of directives that don’t have their own template:

1. **Structural directives** – add/remove DOM elements (e.g., `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`).
2. **Attribute directives** – change the appearance or behavior of an existing element (e.g., `ngClass`, `ngStyle`).

Directives give HTML superpowers – they let you write declarative, dynamic views.

quizData.question: Which of the following is a structural directive?
quizData.explanation: `*ngIf` is structural because it adds or removes elements from the DOM. The asterisk is the clue.

slides.title: Components Are Directives Too! 👀
slides.content:
## Every Component Is a Directive… with a template.

* Components are actually a special kind of directive with a view.
* Under the hood, `@Component` extends `@Directive`.
* So when you write `@Component(...)`, you're creating a directive that owns a template.

But when we talk about “directives” in Angular, we usually mean non‑component directives: structural and attribute directives.

slides.title: Structural vs Attribute: The Key Difference 🔑
slides.content:
| Feature | Structural Directives | Attribute Directives |
|---------|----------------------|----------------------|
| Effect on DOM | Add / remove elements | Modify existing element |
| Syntax | Prefixed with `*` (e.g., `*ngIf`) | Wrapped in `[ ]` (e.g., `[ngStyle]`) |
| Underlying mechanism | Wraps the host in an `<ng-template>` | No extra template |
| Examples | `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch` | `ngClass`, `ngStyle`, custom directives |

## The Asterisk is Syntactic Sugar `*ngIf="condition"` is shorthand for: ```html
Welcome back!
 ``` Understanding this will make advanced template techniques much easier later on.

quizData.question: Attribute directives can add or remove elements from the DOM.
quizData.explanation: Only structural directives can alter the DOM structure. Attribute directives modify existing elements.

slides.title: Built‑In vs Custom Directives 🛠️
slides.content:
## Two Sources of Directives

* **Built‑in**: `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch`, `ngClass`, `ngStyle`, `ngModel` (actually a directive).
* **Custom**: You can create your own structural or attribute directives using `@Directive` decorator.

We’ll explore all the built‑in ones in this chapter and build our own custom directive at the end.
